newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar beats target, bullish on outlook.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar beats target, bullish on outlook.

text.p: A positive outlook for U.S. refining bolstered Ultramar Diamond Shamrock stock after the company reported first quarter earnings some 10 cents per share ahead of analysts' expectations on Tuesday.

The stock rose two to 32-1/2 after Ultramar Diamond Shamrock, which was formed in December 1996, reported a rise in net income to $27.6 million, or $0.35 per share, from a proforma $22.0 million, $0.28 a year ago.
Adjusted for a one-time gain from a property sale, EPS were $0.26, against a First Call consensus of $0.19.
Revenues rose to $2.6 billion from $2.4 billion.

"This is the beginning of a trend where Ultramar starts surprising on the upside. Their inability to do so until now is what has kept the stock at a discount to its peer group," said Ravi Kamath, analyst at Jefferies & Co in Houston.
The company said projected savings from the merger of Ultramar and Diamond Shamrock would be $35 million this year compared with a forecast $25 million, and in excess of $85 million in 1998.

Kamath also identified $50 million a year savings from Ultramar Diamond Shamrock's proposed $811 million acquisition of Total Petroleum (North America) Ltd, although due diligence has not been completed.
The deal will increase refining capacity to 650,000 barrels per day from 500,000 when it is completed this summer.

Ultramar's chief executive Roger Hemminghaus said the second quarter started well after a squeeze in the early part of the first quarter in Texas and that West Coast refining margins, Canadian retail gasoline margins and the Northeast home heating oil business were strong.
Margins in Quebec, however, fell by $1.40 a barrel in the first quarter, more than offsetting an 4,600 barrel per day increase in throughputs.

Retail company operated margins throughout the Southwest dropped to 9.1 cents from 11.4 cents per gallon a year ago, more than offsetting a rise in 3,000 barrels a day in sales. In California, margins averaged only 3.8 cents per gallon during the quarter.
The company has aggressive retail expansion plans and the Total Petroleum deal means the number of retail outlets will rise ot 6,381 from 4,300.
Ultramar will also build 19 new stations this year.

"As a major gasoline/convenience store operator focused on key inland markets, UDS's convenience merchandise sales will increase to more than $1.5 billion per year after this acquisition is completed this summer," Hemminghaus said.

Analysts say the retail strategy will diversify earnings away from the volatile refining sector, although some noted that debt of $1.9 billion leaves the company exposed should refining margins turn down.
Jefferies' Kamath disagrees.
"There is no liquidity issue and certainly no debt service issue," he said.
He is forecasting earnings per share of $2.50 for the full year, up from $1.11 and will look at forecasts later on.
"It looks as if the second quarter will be a very, very good quarter," Kamath said.
((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
